pages.text: The $(item)Chemical Reactor$() has an $(thing)Operation$() console now, like the big physics machines. Set two things: the $(thing)heater temperature$() and the $(thing)residence time$() - how long each batch is held.$(br2)A reaction goes at the rate constant k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT) (Arrhenius): hotter is faster, and the higher its activation energy Eₐ, the more heat it needs.

A batch held for τ reaches the conversion X = 1 − e^(−kτ). Each recipe needs its own conversion (the recipe page shows it); until the readout reaches it the reactor waits, $(thing)Out of Window$().$(br2)A shorter residence time runs more batches (60 s is the normal pace, down to a quarter of it) - so heat it up, then shorten τ until X just reaches the target.

Two limits: the vessel is rated to 850 K, and a recipe with a $(thing)catalyst$() has the catalyst's sintering temperature (700 K). A catalyst lowers Eₐ - the same reaction runs at a much lower temperature - but run it above 700 K and it wears ten times as fast.
